{{Short description|Type of category in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''extensive category''' is a [[category (mathematics)|category]] '''C''' with finite [[coproduct]]s that are disjoint and well-behaved with respect to [[pullback (category theory)|pullback]]s. Equivalently, '''C''' is extensive if the coproduct [[functor]] from the [[product category|product]] of the [[slice category|slice categories]] '''C'''/''X''&nbsp;×&nbsp;'''C'''/''Y'' to the slice category '''C'''/(''X''&nbsp;+&thinsp;''Y'') is an [[equivalence of categories]] for all objects ''X'' and ''Y'' of '''C'''.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Introduction to extensive and distributive categories|journal=[[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]]|volume=84|issue=2|pages=145–158|last1=Carboni|first1=Aurelio|last2=Lack|first2=Stephen|last3=Walters|first3=R.F.C.|doi=10.1016/0022-4049(93)90035-R|year=1993|doi-access=}}</ref>

==Examples==
The categories '''Set''' and '''Top''' of [[set (mathematics)|set]]s and [[topological space]]s, respectively, are extensive categories.<ref name="cite2">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WHudOFwuMn8C&pg=PA342|title=Categorical Foundations: Special Topics in Order, Topology, Algebra, and Sheaf Theory|last1=Pedicchio|first1=Maria Cristina|author1-link=M. Cristina Pedicchio|last2=Tholen|first2=Walter|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-83414-8|access-date=4 April 2018|year=2004}}</ref> More generally, the category of presheaves on any [[small category]] is extensive.<ref name="cite2" />

The category '''CRing'''<sup>op</sup> of [[affine scheme]]s is extensive.
